note: VAPN (View access per node) controls the VIEW operation on nodes only. You enable it per content type on its settings form (config vapn.settings, key 'bundles' = map of bundle->true; configure route vapn.settings at /admin/config/people/vapn). For each enabled bundle it attaches a code-defined 'vapn' field (unlimited entity-reference to user_role) shown as a vertical tab on the node form. hook_node_access(): a node with roles selected is viewable only by users holding one of those roles; no roles selected = VAPN abstains (neutral). Permissions: administer vapn (settings + field edit), use vapn (field edit), bypass vapn (always view). Medium/hard cases are grounded in the live vapn.settings config (the map of enabled bundles), which is the module's stable, exportable state: inspect which bundles are enabled, and enable VAPN on one or more content types, verified against live config.

evals.prompt: I installed the VAPN (View access per node) module in Drupal. How do I turn on per-node view access for a content type, and where is that stored in configuration?
evals.expected_output: Go to /admin/config/people/vapn (route vapn.settings, needs 'administer vapn') and tick the content types. It is stored in the vapn.settings config object under 'bundles' as a map of enabled bundle machine name => true (e.g. bundles.article: true). Each enabled bundle then gets a 'View access per node' field on the node form.

evals.prompt: With the VAPN module, how is view access to a node decided? What happens if a node has no roles selected, and which permission lets someone bypass the restriction?
evals.expected_output: VAPN only affects the 'view' operation. If a node has one or more roles selected, only users with at least one of those roles may view it; if no roles are selected VAPN abstains (neutral) and leaves access to core/other modules. Users with the 'bypass vapn' permission can always view.

evals.prompt: Does the VAPN module control who can edit or delete a node, or just who can view it? What is the machine name of the field it adds to each node?
evals.expected_output: VAPN only controls the 'view' operation (via hook_node_access) — it does not affect create, update, or delete. On enabled content types it adds a 'vapn' field, an unlimited entity-reference to user_role, listing the roles allowed to view that node.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, which content type(s) currently have VAPN (View access per node) enabled? Inspect the live VAPN configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: The 'article' content type. The vapn.settings config object has bundles.article = true (bundles is the map of content types VAPN applies to).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, list every content type that currently has VAPN (View access per node) enabled. Inspect the live VAPN configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: Both the 'article' and 'page' content types. The vapn.settings config object has bundles.article = true and bundles.page = true.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the VAPN module to enable per-node view access on the 'article' content type. Apply the change to the live configuration so that Article nodes get the 'View access per node' field.
evals.expected_output: Set vapn.settings 'bundles' so that bundles.article is true (via the VAPN settings form at /admin/config/people/vapn, or by editing the config), then clear cached field definitions so the vapn field attaches to Article.

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site I want to control view access per node on BOTH my Articles and my Basic pages. Using the VAPN module, turn on per-node view access for both the 'article' and 'page' content types, and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable both content types in vapn.settings so bundles.article and bundles.page are true (tick Article and Basic page on /admin/config/people/vapn, or set both keys in the config), then clear cached field definitions so the vapn field attaches to both.
